title: Three perfect days in Las Vegas: Halloween on the Strip and downtown
dek: A Nevada Day hockey matinee, Metallica inside Sphere on Halloween night, a morning among the red cliffs and a Día de los Muertos Sunday downtown, with an extra hour of sleep thrown in.

hero.caption: The Las Vegas Strip, where most of Friday and Saturday night play out.

intro:
Las Vegas never needs an excuse to dress up, but this weekend it gets three. Friday, October 30, is **Nevada Day**, the state holiday, and the Golden Knights mark it with a 3 p.m. matinee against the New Jersey Devils at T-Mobile Arena. Saturday is Halloween, and the city has stacked its biggest names on the same night: Metallica playing the next show of its no-repeats *Life Burns Faster* residency inside Sphere, Doja Cat and Latto at T-Mobile Arena, and UNLV hosting Northern Illinois at Allegiant Stadium. Sunday brings the city's free Día de los Muertos festival to the lawn of the Civic Center downtown, with seven community altars, music and food.

The heat is gone. Late October is the season locals wait for, when you can walk between resorts at noon and the desert west of town is pleasant enough for a long morning drive. The National Weather Service did flag some uncertainty for Halloween weekend, with a 10 to 50 percent chance of showers and stronger southwest winds if a system arrives, so this plan keeps most of its hours indoors and puts the one desert outing first thing Saturday, when it can be moved.

The shape of the weekend: Friday in the middle of the Strip, from the Bellagio Conservatory's autumn cabin to the hockey and an evening at Sphere. Saturday out to Red Rock Canyon and back through Chinatown for dumplings and charcoal-grilled skewers before the Halloween crowds take over the boulevard. Sunday downtown and in the Arts District, where the old Vegas of mob trials and neon signs sits a few blocks from some of the city's best cooking. Clocks fall back an hour early Sunday, so the last day starts with a gift.

days.title: Friday: the center Strip on Nevada Day
days.intro: Breakfast under the Bellagio glass, a hockey matinee and a night inside the Sphere.

stops.name: Sadelle's
stops.text: The New York bagel house runs a sunny all-day dining room inside Bellagio, and breakfast is the meal to have here. The Infatuation steers you to the bagel towers, the soft scrambled eggs (with trout roe or caviar if you are feeling flush) and a brûléed grapefruit cocktail; grab a sticky bun from the cart by the door on your way out. It is not cheap, so treat it as the weekend's long, lazy breakfast. Book through SevenRooms, since a holiday Friday on the Strip fills tables early.

stops.name: Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens
stops.text: This fall's display, designed by Ed Libby, is a woodland retreat built around a New England coastal cabin, with woodland animals sculpted from 8,300 pounds of manzanita and driftwood, about 500,000 autumn leaves, some 37,800 fall flowers and plants and a 687-pound pumpkin. It is free and open around the clock, so go mid-morning before the tour groups arrive. Inside the cabin, The Garden Table seats diners for brunch from Sadelle's and dinner from Michael Mina, by reservation only.

stops.name: Eataly Las Vegas
stops.text: A short walk south, the Italian food hall at Park MGM is the easy pre-game lunch: Roman-style pizza, fresh pasta, a long counter of cheeses and cured meats, and a market with thousands of products if you want to take olive oil home. Its newer corners, opened in 2025, are the horseshoe-shaped Eataly Bar and Pizza al Padellino, an open-kitchen pizzeria, both on the lower level. No booking needed for the counters, and T-Mobile Arena is across the plaza when you are done.
stops.addr: 3770 S Las Vegas Blvd (inside Park MGM)

stops.name: Golden Knights vs. New Jersey Devils
stops.text: The Golden Knights, now in their 10th season, play a Nevada Day matinee against the Devils at 3 p.m. Vegas does hockey with a show-business pregame, and a daytime puck drop means you see it and still have the whole evening free. Buy through the team's single-game ticket page or Ticketmaster rather than street resellers, and arrive 45 minutes early: the arena bag policy is strict and the security lines build quickly on a holiday.

stops.name: Bavette's Steakhouse & Bar
stops.text: Back across the plaza, the Chicago steakhouse at Park MGM is dark, clubby and very good. Haute Living's 2025 roundup points you to the USDA Prime ribeye or bone-in filet with béarnaise or cognac peppercorn sauce, crab-stuffed avocado or steak tartare to start, and pommes purée on the side. The French-leaning wine list rewards a question to the sommelier. Book well ahead for a Friday; an early table leaves time to reach Sphere for the 8 p.m. show.
stops.addr: 3770 S Las Vegas Blvd (inside Park MGM)

stops.name: The Wizard of Oz at Sphere
stops.text: Sphere's expanded *Wizard of Oz* is the city's most talked-about screening, and this weekend it gets a Halloween treatment: from Friday to Sunday the atrium has themed concessions, trick-or-treat stations, a 3D haunted-forest photo spot and a commemorative treat bag, with an afterparty following Friday's 8 p.m. show. Costumes are welcome but masks are not, under venue rules. Take a cab or the monorail up the Strip, and buy through Sphere's Halloween page.

days.title: Saturday: red rock, Chinatown and Halloween night
days.intro: Out to the cliffs early, dumplings and robata on Spring Mountain Road, then the loudest night of the year.

stops.name: Red Rock Canyon Scenic Drive
stops.area: Red Rock Canyon, west of the city
stops.text: West of the city, the 13-mile Scenic Drive loops beneath the red and cream sandstone of the Red Rock escarpment, with pullouts for short walks and photographs. From October 1 to May 31 you need a timed-entry reservation from Recreation.gov for any entry between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., so book your slot before you leave home; the drive is open until 7 p.m. in October. The visitor center opens at 8 a.m. If the forecast showers arrive, swap this for a late-morning museum and come back Sunday.
stops.wiki: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area

stops.name: Ellie's Chinese Restaurant
stops.text: On the drive back, Spring Mountain Road turns into Las Vegas's Chinatown, a long run of strip malls that holds some of the best eating in town. Ellie's, one of the Review-Journal's picks among this year's new Chinatown openings, does barbecued pork buns, stir-fried rice noodle rolls in XO sauce, ma la boiled beef and its signature crisp-fried rice noodles. Order a few plates to share; this is the meal that sets you up for a long night.

stops.name: Raku
stops.text: After an afternoon off at the hotel, come back to Chinatown for the Japanese robata bar that Las Vegas chefs eat at after their own shifts. Raku grills over binchotan charcoal imported from Japan and is known for oden and skewers; the premium or deluxe omakase moves from house-made tofu through sashimi, grilled meats and the day's fish. Call at least three days ahead for omakase, or book a table on Resy, and pick from the long sake list.

stops.name: Metallica: Life Burns Faster at Sphere
stops.text: Metallica's Sphere residency promises no repeated setlists across its paired nights, and October 29 and 31 are this week's pair, so Halloween gets its own show at 8:30 p.m. Expect resale prices; if you are not going, the other big ticket is Doja Cat with Latto at T-Mobile Arena at 7:30. Either way, the Strip itself is the show afterward, with costumed crowds on the sidewalks until late. Leave the car at the hotel and walk or ride the monorail.

days.title: Sunday: downtown and the Arts District
days.intro: An extra hour, brunch on Main Street, mob history, the Day of the Dead and old neon at dusk.

stops.name: Esther's Kitchen
stops.text: Chef James Trees, a Las Vegas native and a 2026 James Beard semifinalist, makes nearly everything in house at his Arts District Italian, and OpenTable named it one of the country's top brunch spots this year. Look for the pasta fritti with eggs, the smoked ocean trout toast and a brunch pizza, plus the bread. The restaurant moved in 2024 to a larger, 187-seat room on South Main Street. Book through the restaurant or OpenTable; with the clock change you will have time to spare.

stops.name: The Mob Museum
stops.text: Steps from Fremont Street, the Mob Museum tells the story of organized crime in Las Vegas and the law enforcement that pursued it, and it is the best history lesson in town on how this city got built. Allow a couple of hours. Downstairs, The Underground speakeasy and distillery opens at 11 a.m. on Sundays for a drink in period style. Open daily 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.; buying online saves up to 20 percent.

stops.name: Día de los Muertos Festival
stops.text: A few blocks away, the City of Las Vegas fills the Civic Center lawn from 1 to 7 p.m. with a free festival: seven community-built ofrendas, including altars from Chicanos Por La Causa and Clark County Family Services Foster Care, live music, free face painting and artisan stalls. Food comes from local vendors such as Tacos La Estancia, Don Carnitas and La Churrera, with drinks from Aguas Frescas 702. Bring a blanket or a low-back chair, and pick up a festival passport to stamp.

stops.name: The Neon Museum
stops.text: The boneyard of retired casino signs opens at 3 p.m. through May, and the clock change pulls sunset an hour earlier today, so a late-afternoon ticket lets you see the paint and lettering in daylight and the restored signs switch on as it gets dark. Evening entry costs more than daytime. Add the guided tour for the stories behind the signs, or the 25-minute *Brilliant!* projection show. The box office closes an hour before closing; book ahead.

stops.name: Carson Kitchen
stops.text: In the old John E. Carson Hotel, this small-plates kitchen is the downtown dinner locals send visitors to. Share grilled oysters Rockefeller, the ginger pear salad with brie and pecans, the "Devil's" eggs and tempura green beans, then a pork chop with sage beurre blanc. Sunday service runs until 10 p.m. Book online, since the room is small and fills before shows on Fremont.

stops.name: Fremont Street Experience
stops.text: End where Las Vegas started, under the canopy over Fremont Street. Viva Vision, the giant overhead screen, runs a free six-to-eight-minute music-and-light show at the top of every hour from 6 p.m. to 2 a.m. Catch the 8 o'clock, then wander the old casinos, the Golden Nugget and the El Cortez among them, and on toward Fremont East's bars. It is loud and tacky in the best way, and a fitting last look before the airport.
stops.addr: Fremont St between Main St and 4th St

stay.name: Wynn Las Vegas
stay.text: The polished north end of the Strip, and the most decorated hotel in town. Wynn Tower Suites marked its 20th straight year of Forbes Five-Star recognition in 2026, and the Spa at Wynn holds five stars too. It is a cab ride to Sphere and an easy one to downtown on Sunday.

stay.name: Bellagio
stay.text: The fountains, the Conservatory's autumn cabin downstairs and Sadelle's for breakfast: Friday's plan barely leaves the building, and T-Mobile Arena and Park MGM are a short walk south. A classic choice for a first visit.

stay.name: El Cortez
stay.text: Founded in 1941 and celebrating its 85th year, El Cortez is the only continuously operating casino listed on the National Register of Historic Places. It puts you a short walk from the Mob Museum, the Fremont Street canopy and Sunday's festival, at downtown prices.

events.name: The Wizard of Oz at Sphere: Halloween celebration
events.text: Trick-or-treat stations, themed concessions and a haunted-forest photo spot in the atrium for showgoers Oct. 30 to Nov. 1; costumes welcome, no masks.

events.name: Metallica: Life Burns Faster
events.text: The Halloween show in Metallica's no-repeats Sphere residency, which also plays Thursday, Oct. 29.

events.name: Doja Cat with Latto: Tour Ma Vie
events.text: Doja Cat brings her biggest tour yet to the Strip on Halloween night.

events.name: UNLV vs. Northern Illinois
events.text: A Mountain West home game for the Rebels; expect heavy traffic on I-15 and around the south Strip.

events.name: The Phantom of the Opera
events.text: The touring Phantom closes its Oct. 21 to Nov. 1 run in the Smith Center's Broadway series.

events.name: Día de los Muertos Festival
events.where: Las Vegas Civic Center, 525 S. Main St.
events.text: Free city festival with seven community ofrendas, music, food and artisan vendors, face painting and a stamp passport.

know: From Harry Reid International Airport (LAS), a taxi takes 10 to 20 minutes to the Strip, at flat zone rates of roughly $21 to $30 plus a card fee; rideshare pickups are in the parking garages. The Centennial Express (CX) bus runs from both terminals to downtown.

RTC passes for the Strip and all routes, including the 24-hour Deuce bus between the Strip and downtown, cost $6 for two hours, $8 for 24 hours and $20 for three days; buy in the rideRTC app. The Las Vegas Monorail runs along the east side of the Strip.
Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 1: clocks go back one hour. Check your flight time and any Sunday booking against the new time, and expect sunset an hour earlier.

Friday is Nevada Day, a state holiday; state offices are closed. Saturday night stacks Metallica at Sphere, Doja Cat at T-Mobile Arena and UNLV football at Allegiant Stadium, so plan on slow traffic around the Strip and long ride-share waits after 10 p.m.
Tipping runs 15 to 20 percent at restaurants and for taxis; a dollar or two a drink at bars.
Red Rock Canyon needs a timed-entry reservation from Oct. 1 to May 31 for entry between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.; book on Recreation.gov in advance.
The forecast carries a 10 to 50 percent chance of showers and gusty southwest winds around Halloween; pack a light layer for evenings.
